text:
Recent work supports evaluating recommendation evidence separately from explanation fluency. [Factual Consistency (2025, revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366) finds strong semantic similarity can coexist with poor statement-level factual precision. [ECCR (2024)](https://www.amazon.science/publications/eccr-explainable-and-coherent-complement-recommendation-based-on-large-language-models) treats coherent complements as both compatible and relevant: broad topical relatedness alone does not establish usefulness together. [Abstention-Aware Scientific Reasoning (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14189), from an adjacent domain, offers a transferable pattern: decompose claims into conditions, check each against evidence, then support, refute, or abstain.

A practical adaptation is a recommendation-level rubric with separate judgments for specific history match versus broad relatedness; useful complement versus substitute or duplicate; and prerequisite/compatibility status: supported, contradicted, unknown, or not applicable. Retain item IDs, history anchors, exact title/description spans, and a brief rationale for every judgment. Require explicit evidence for model, format, connector, or dependency compatibility; missing evidence means unknown, not incompatible. An interaction establishes observed engagement, not ownership, satisfaction, or an unobserved personality trait. These are proposed operational rules, not a validated rubric from the cited papers.

For the twenty observed users, audit a fixed recommendation depth across all four categories, with independent annotations and adjudication where feasible. Report agreement, evidence-supported judgment rates, contradiction rates, duplicate/complement rates, and unknown rates with explicit denominators; preserve per-category results. Check rubric judgments against supplied feedback without claiming new user confirmation. Treat this small audit as diagnostic evidence, while retaining macro validation HR@10 for model selection. No user-level validation was performed in this search.
